findings.reason: if the acknowledgement was for the right run and the row persisted, the defect is in the deferral read or the row's run id, and a node would implement a charge fix that leaves the coordinator unable to clear the stop hook the section exists to remove.
findings.text: §53 quotes "crew ack from nova-00 returned ok and the row stayed outstanding" and attributes that to the obligation being charged to the dispatching session, but the acknowledgement path withholds a run's duties by run id for every session (`_partition_acknowledged` at reckon/crew/obligations.py:2055-2063 over `_acknowledgements_in_force` at reckon/crew/obligations.py:1968-2025, keyed on `item.get("run_id")`), so an acknowledgement naming the held run would have deferred the row whichever session it was charged to; the note records neither the run id nova-00 acknowledged nor the deferral that was written, so the cited evidence is equally consistent with the row carrying a different run id from the one acknowledged or with the deferral read failing, and the stated root cause is not shown.

findings.reason: the node's done-when must state the observable a deferral actually produces (the row leaves the outstanding list until the recorded instant, in the holder's slice) and name the module that records it, or the node fails the case or widens its scope silently.
findings.text: the case "B's acknowledgement retires it" cannot be satisfied by `crew ack --run`, which requires `--until` and records a deferral that withholds a run's obligations until that instant rather than retiring them (option guard `if not until: raise click.ClickException("--run requires --until")` and `record_run_acknowledgement` at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2360-2370, reckon/crew/runs.py:3045-3083), and neither reckon/crew_run_commands.py nor reckon/crew/runs.py is among §53's write paths, so the case is either unsatisfiable as written or forces the node into an undeclared module.
